newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin sees IPB selloff in weeks after probe.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin sees IPB selloff in weeks after probe.

text.p: The sale of a state stake in Czech bank IPB a.s. to Japan's Nomura should be completed within weeks, Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said on Thursday.

Speaking at a news conference, Pilip said negotiations on the sale of the state's 36 percent stake in IPB, the country's third largest bank, would only end after an investigation into the bank's investment fund arm is completed.

"Very intensive (privatisation) negotiations are being held, and we believe that in a short time we will be able to announce a significant advancement," Pilip said. "I firmly believe it (the selloff) will be in the range of weeks."

The government has said it will sell its stake in IPB -- held by the National Property Fund (NPF) and post service Ceska Posta s.p. -- and recently charged the Finance Ministry to negotiate exclusively with Nomura on the sale.

Nomura already controls a five percent stake in IPB through the Czech- registered firm Nutshell s.r.o.. It has held as much as 10 percent of IPB, but recently let go of half of its holdings as part of a repurchase operation with shareholders.
Pilip said that his ministry's capital market supervision would finish the probe at IPB's investment subsidiary, Prvni Investicni a.s. (PIAS), prior to the privatisation.

PIAS is the Czech Republic's largest fund manager. It has come under fire in local media from some shareholders of funds it manages for alleged unfair practices and trades unfavourable to the shareholders.
Pilip said on Thursday the ministry would finish analysing the outcome of its control in PIAS soon and take action if necessary.
"The conclusions (of the probe) will be finalised before the negotiation with the party interested in buying the state stake ends," the minister said.
"At the moment when (the ministry) finally analyses the discovered shortfalls which are being talked about, it will take steps corresponding to the seriousness (of these)," he added.

The privatisation process of IPB had already hit a bump when police arrested the bank's general director Jiri Tesar and his deputy for alleged fraud. The two have since been released from jail, but an investigation into the case continues.
Tesar, who stepped down as director at IPB's Thursday's annual general meeting, said earlier in the day the the privatisation process should be finalised by the end of summer.
